one_liner: Senior TSA contract specialist (GS-14 equivalent) in Springfield who plans major acquisitions, runs contract administration, interprets procurement policy and mentors junior contracting staff.
fit_summary: This is a senior 1102 contracting role. It requires four years of contracting experience, one year directing full contract administration (modifications, claims, contractor performance appraisals), a bachelor's degree with 24 business-related semester hours, and FAC-C (Professional) certification. Daniel's file shows emergency-management consulting and policy strengths, but nothing confirming hands-on contracting experience, the required coursework, or FAC-C. Unless Daniel has those, Daniel will likely be rated ineligible.
eligibility: Open to the public under Direct Hire Authority, so no federal status or veterans' preference is needed.

You need one year of specialized experience at SV-I/GS-13 level covering all four areas: full-range contract administration, interpreting complex contracting policy, major acquisition planning, and mentoring others in contract execution. You also need four years of progressively responsible contracting experience.

You need a bachelor's degree that includes at least 24 semester hours in accounting, business, finance, law, contracts, purchasing, economics, management or similar fields, and you must submit transcripts by the closing date.
FAC-C (Professional) certification or equivalent must be verified.
You must obtain a Secret clearance and a favorable background investigation, file a financial disclosure, be a U.S. citizen, and be registered with Selective Service.
strategy: Before applying, check yourself honestly against all four specialized-experience elements and the FAC-C and coursework requirements. If any one is missing, skip this posting rather than overstate, because overstating can get you removed from consideration.

If your IEM role involved contract work for government clients (proposal pricing, task order management, modifications, subcontractor oversight), describe it in the posting's exact language with month/year dates and 40 hours per week, all within the two-page limit.

Since the notice reposts quarterly, treat it as a long-term target if you're not ready. Consider entry-level 1102 roles (GS-7/9 or pathways), FAC-C training through FAI, and filling coursework gaps to build toward this level.

Answer the questionnaire honestly (preview it at the posted link) and get ready for the USA Hire assessments, which have a cut score; play to your strengths in interpersonal skills, negotiating and customer service.
Gather transcripts and your FAC-C certificate before the window opens, and submit by November 5, 2026.
resume_bullets: Managed contract administration for [number] [contract type] contracts valued at [$amount] for [government client], issuing [number] modifications and resolving [type of] contractor delays.
Interpreted [FAR/agency] contracting policies to resolve [specific issue] on [program], recommending [approach] adopted by [client/leadership].
Mentored [number] junior staff on contract execution and administration, including [specific tasks such as subcontractor surveillance or performance appraisals].
interview_questions: Walk us through how you handled a contract claim or dispute from start to finish.
How have you planned a major acquisition so it met timeliness and functionality needs?
Tell us about a time you interpreted an ambiguous contracting policy and developed a new approach.
How do you coach less-experienced specialists or CORs to improve their performance?
watch_outs: The specialized experience, degree coursework and FAC-C requirements are strict, and nothing on file confirms Daniel meets them.
The role requires a Secret clearance and financial disclosure.
Each application window is short (October 22 to November 5, 2026), though the notice reposts quarterly.
